evidence.section: 3.2 Cause of lamellar spacing dependence of creep rate
evidence.quote: The decrease of creep rate in the primary creep stage is due to strain hardening, and becomes more significant with the decreasing lamellar spacing.

The discontinuous coarsening (bulging type DRX) is accompanied by migration of interphase and/or grain boundaries. The migrating boundaries sweep away dislocations which caused the strain hardening in the primary creep, resulting in the softening during the tertiary creep.
The spheroidization (nucle- ation type dynamic recrystallization (DRX)) has been reported by other researchers,10,’ 1 and is known to increase creep rate of fully lamellar TiAl alloys.

evidence.section: 3.2 Cause of lamellar spacing dependence of creep rate
evidence.quote: The decrease of creep rate in the primary creep stage is due to strain hardening, and becomes more significant with the decreasing lamellar spacing.
The prominent discontinuous coarsening of the fine lamellar structure at the low stresses is responsible for the rapid creep acceleration
The migrating boundaries sweep away dislocations which caused the strain hardening in the primary creep, resulting in the softening during the tertiary creep.
The spheroidization (nucle- ation type dynamic recrystallization (DRX)) has been reported by other researchers,10,’ 1 and is known to increase creep rate of fully lamellar TiAl alloys.
is known to increase creep rate of fully lamellar TiAl alloys
The area fractions of DRX region formed during creep of Sp.Al and A2 are included in Fig. 3, indicating that the sta- bilization suppresses DRX during creep.
Creep acceleration in the ter- tiary creep stage, namely dlns/dt decreases with increasing area fraction of prior DC region, because of the suppression of DRX during creep.
These results confirm the expectation that the strengthening by fine lamellar structure becomes effective at low stresses when DC is prevented by stabilization prior to creep.
